test_title: PYST 48: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 03 Sept, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What was one of the key effects of globalisation on the Indian economy after 1991?

options.text: Entry of foreign companies and capital

solution:
The correct answer is __**Entry of foreign companies and capital**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Globalisation in India began with the **economic reforms of 1991**, which marked the liberalisation of the Indian economy by reducing trade barriers and encouraging foreign investments.
 
• One of the key outcomes of globalisation was the **entry of multinational corporations (MNCs)** and foreign capital into various sectors, including manufacturing, IT, banking, and retail.
 
• The Indian government allowed **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** in several industries, which led to an influx of foreign companies establishing operations in India.
 
• This increased foreign capital helped in improving infrastructure, generating employment, and enhancing technological advancements across industries.
 
• Globalisation also facilitated **technology transfer** from developed nations, boosting productivity and innovation in the Indian economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reduction in foreign exchange reserves (Option 1):**

 
 
• Before the 1991 reforms, India faced a severe **foreign exchange crisis**, with reserves dwindling to just two weeks’ worth of imports.
 
• However, post-liberalisation, foreign exchange reserves increased significantly due to foreign investment and export growth.
 
• Thus, globalisation actually helped improve reserves rather than reducing them.
 
 
 
• **Closure of Indian banks (Option 3):**
 
 
• Globalisation did not lead to the closure of Indian banks; instead, it encouraged reforms in the banking sector.
 
• Indian banks adopted modern technologies, improved operational efficiency, and expanded globally.
 
• Private sector banks like ICICI and HDFC Bank emerged stronger during this period.
 
 
 
• **Decrease in exports (Option 4):**
 
 
• Globalisation led to an **increase in exports** as Indian businesses gained access to international markets.
 
• India's export sector expanded in areas like IT services, textiles, and pharmaceuticals.
 
• Trade liberalisation policies and reduced tariffs further boosted export performance.
